From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-12-13T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Priority triage: week of 2026-12-13 — wins / risks / asks (QBR prep + OKR check)

Team — quick read for the week. This is the consolidated leadership readout for OKR check-ins and QBR prep; please scan and action where assigned. I’ve attached a working QBR deck and the runbook table.

Wins:
- Serving runtime P95 latency improved 12% vs last week on our standard text-gen trace (from 360ms -> 318ms) after the kernel selector tweaks.
- Cost per token (median customer mix) down ~9% after batching/kv-cache changes; early Dedicated customers showing 7–10% unit cost wins.
- New trial conversion: Aurora test cluster converted to a pilot environment; initial throughput matches our SLO in Canary.

Risks / open issues:
1) Quantized 4-bit rollout created a small eval drift on our summarization benchmark — mean ROUGE drop ~0.04 (≈4% relative). We need a mitigation plan if this persists in the QBR sample set. Owner: @aditya_rao.
2) SOC2 evidence packet: Aurora has requested retention tables and audit-log exports; legal/procurement timelines could push contract signature past our usual pilot window. Owner: @laura_bennett.
3) Dedicated capacity lead time: procurement for additional A100 nodes may be 6–8 weeks if we don’t commit this week; that delays guaranteed throughput for Aurora expansion. Owner: @karthik_iyer.

Asks (actionable items):
- Approve a 6-week pilot discount (proposed 20% off list) to expedite Aurora conversion to Dedicated. (Decision needed by Thu 12/16). Assigned: @laura_bennett.
- Aditya: please produce a short evaluation slide (1) showing before/after quantization metrics, (2) a short mitigation plan if ROUGE delta > 0.03. Due: Wed 12/15 EOD.
- Karthik: confirm procurement ETA and alternate capacity plan (burst to hosted region vs reserved nodes). Due: Thu 12/16 morning.
- Ops: finalize the rollback runbook table I attached and call out the exact metric thresholds for automatic fallback during the QBR demo. Owner: @aditya_rao + @sofia_ivanova.

Quick numbers for OKR check (week over week):
- Platform reliability (SLO >= 99.8%) — current: 99.86% (on track)
- Latency P95 — improved 12% (as above)
- Cost/unit — improved 9%
- Trial -> pilot conversion rate — +1.8pp MoM (need additional Enterprise conversions to hit target)

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v3.pdf (working slides), okrs-weekly-snapshot.csv (numbers), qbr-runbook-rollback-table.csv (runbook).

If there are objections to the pilot discount or a call for a different escalation path, flag now. I’ll be compiling a one-page QBR 'ask' slide for the exec deck by Wednesday morning.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
VP, Platform & Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Priority triage: week of 2026-12-13 — wins / risks / asks (QBR prep + OKR check)

Acknowledged. Quick responses:

- Quantization drift: I reproduced the ROUGE delta locally against the curated QBR prompt set. The 4% relative drop is concentrated in corner cases with aggressive truncation; median performance unchanged. Immediate mitigation options: (A) selective per-layer fp16 for last two decoder layers (low perf hit), (B) thresholded fallback to fp16 for prompts labeled high-risk.
- I’ll own the evaluation slide. Plan: two slides — one with before/after aggregate metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, hallucination proxy), second with the mitigation matrix + perf tradeoffs. ETA: Wed 12/15 17:00 PT.
- Ops runbook: I’ll update the CSV with the exact detection thresholds and the canary rollback hook.

FYI — I’ve looped in Raj (cc’d internally to the infra team) to ensure the kernel selector change can be toggled during the QBR demo without a full redeploy.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Applied ML, Redwood Inference
